_what: Host globals that verify-no-undefined-names.mjs treats as defined. ECMAScript's own globals are listed in that file instead, so it is always clear which names are the language's and which belong to Foundry or the browser.
_howGenerated: Read off a RUNNING Foundry client, not written by hand. Every name below was confirmed present in globalThis on the live world at localhost:30000 on 23 August 2026. A hand-written list is a guess about someone else's API surface, and every name it forgets becomes a false positive that trains the reader to ignore this check.
_scope: THIS IS AN INTERSECTION, NOT THE WHOLE SURFACE. The live client exposes 1863 globals; recorded here are only the 22 that this codebase actually references, each verified to exist. The tradeoff, stated plainly because the anti-silence rule requires it: a genuinely undefined name always fails, which is what this check is for — but the FIRST use of a legitimate Foundry global that is not yet on this list will also fail. That is a false positive. It is loud, it names the identifier, and the fix is one line. The opposite tradeoff — a permissive list — would let a real crash through, which is the failure this check exists to prevent (see lesson 5.2, shieldedStrideBonus).
_regenerate: node tools/generate-foundry-globals.mjs --add <name> [...] after confirming in a live client that the name exists, or re-run the browser snippet in that file's header against a running world.
